conventions: The gentilic בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי arrives as two Ngmsa tokens, the second carrying lemma הַ. It is aligned by token and not fused: בֵּית → Beth, and the article-bearing second token → the lehemite, headed on lehemite (16.1, 16.18).

A construct chain the ASV renders by a single English class noun that writes the construct's lexeme and only implies the rectum's — עֶגְלַת בָּקָר → a heifer (16.2), גְּדִי עִזִּים → kid (16.20), and נֹשֵׂא כֵלִים → armorbearer (16.21), where both lexemes are written — is one unit under rule 30 headed on the construct, the supplied a joining it under rule 15; the rectum is not marked unrepresented beside it. Where the ASV writes a word for each (kid of the goats, bearer of armor) rule 2 splits the pair as usual.

The three asterisked ASV supplies in this chapter — Jehovah seeth (16.7, one unit with its subject under rule 2), laden (16.20) and the first evil of 16.23, which stands before רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים where the Hebrew writes no adjective — are each their own added unit; the packet records no variant unit in any of those slots, so rule 53's excluded-reading case does not arise. The second evil of 16.23 is רָעָה's own word.

The impersonal predications טוֹב לְ and רָוַח לְ that the ASV recasts personally (thou shalt be well, Saul was refreshed, was well) give the verb its predicate with whatever auxiliaries the ASV writes, leave the לְ unrepresented under rule 40, and give the suffix the subject pronoun where one is written (16.16 ךְ → thou) and nothing where the ASV lets the clause share an earlier subject (16.23 לוֹ → and was well, suffix unrepresented).

The presentative frame it came to pass / it shall come to pass is headed on pass in all three occurrences (16.6, 16.16, 16.23), with the apodosis that going to the apodosis waw under rule 45 and the temporal בְּ taking when under rule 52; came is the competing head and is named in the 16.6 note.
report: Checked all 46 candidate lemmas and read the dump end to end for added units. Every difference in the table is licensed by a different ASV rendering: the unrepresented waws (16.2 apodosis opened bare, 16.13 וָמָעְלָה), the silenced prepositions (קרא לְ/אֶל, בחר בְּ, רעה בְּ, the dative לְ of provided me / thou shalt be well / was refreshed / was well), the articles (generic הָאָדָם bare, that day, toponym Ramah), and the two נַעַר renderings (thy children / the young men) are each what the ASV wrote.

Recurring constructions are treated one way throughout: the gentilic בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי split by token (16.1, 16.18); the attributive participle יֹדֵעַ / מֵיטִיב taking the supplied relative and copula while the infinitive keeps its own words (16.16, 16.17, 16.18); לִפְנֵי fused (16.8, 16.10, 16.21, 16.22, and 16.16 with the ASV's relative frame); the presentative frame headed on pass with the apodosis that on the apodosis waw (16.6, 16.16, 16.23); the impersonal טוֹב לְ / רָוַח לְ recast personally (16.16, 16.23); the three asterisked ASV supplies all added (16.7, 16.20, 16.23); construct chains rendered by one class noun fused on the construct (16.2, 16.20, 16.21).

Two units are ties the verse pass named and I left standing: 16.4 came marked added beside חָרַד → trembling (came ... trembling as one rendering was the alternative), and 16.20 אֶחָד → a (giving a to the noun under rule 15 was the alternative). Neither recurs in the chapter, so neither is a split.

BSB disagreements: all 27 are documented convention differences — bare-object prepositions, unrendered articles, object markers, the paragogic he on שִׁלְחָה (tagged Sh, not Sd, so rule 32's first sentence governs), the two compound-preposition waws, and the 16.23 suffix left without a pronoun where the ASV shares the subject Saul. No genuine error.

No promotion: the chapter's one arguably general lesson (construct + rectum rendered by a single English class noun that writes the construct's lexeme) is already within rule 30's one-rendering condition and I have no corpus counts for גְּדִי עִזִּים or עֶגְלַת בָּקָר to carry a rule; recorded as a chapter convention instead.
